review.summary: changes_needed. The workflow and respond.py changes are sound, but the branch no longer merges: main (via #6/#7) edited the same spots. F1: .gitignore, BACKLOG.md, CHANGELOG.md and reviews/decisions.md all conflict with main; the PR text's "merge cleanly in either order" is stale. F2: the review checkout replaces the PR's respond.py, tests and decisions.md with main's, so the 3 new tests never ran here (83 pass, link checker bad 9 from main's log). F3: always() also runs the archive and artifact steps after a cancel; !cancelled() is the usual guard.

findings.title: Branch conflicts with main in .gitignore, BACKLOG.md, CHANGELOG.md and reviews/decisions.md
findings.claim: The PR description says "#7 removes the same files, and both PRs merge cleanly in either order". That was true of the .pyc deletions, but since #9 was merged into this branch and #6/#7 into main, both sides edit the same lines of four text files, so GitHub will report conflicts and the merge resolution needs care (the decision log must keep both the PR6 and PR8 rows).
findings.evidence: git merge-base HEAD origin/main = 6e0a4cb. `git diff 6e0a4cb origin/main` adds .gitignore with 2 lines (`__pycache__/`, `*.pyc`); this PR adds it with 3 (plus `.pytest_cache/`): add/add with different content. Main replaced BACKLOG.md line 6 "*Nothing deferred yet.*" with two PR6 items; this PR replaces the same line with three PR8 items. Main appended two CHANGELOG lines after the 2026-10-22 anonymise line; this PR appends at the same spot. Main inserted PR6-F1..F9 rows under the decisions.md header; this PR inserts PR8-F1..F6 there. (git merge-tree could not be run in this session; the four overlaps were confirmed from the two diffs.)
findings.proposed_change: Merge origin/main into this branch before it is merged. Resolve: .gitignore = the three-line version; BACKLOG.md = all five items, PR8 items above PR6; CHANGELOG.md = all 2026-10-22 lines, #6/#7 lines before this PR's; reviews/decisions.md = PR8 rows above the PR6 rows (newest first), header untouched. Then update the PR description. Test: `git merge origin/main` reports no conflicts, `python -m pytest -q tests` passes, `python3 tools/check_links.py .` reports bad 0.

findings.title: Reviewer checkout replaces the PR's respond.py, tests and decision log with main's, so the new tests never run
findings.claim: The review workflow checks out main's copies of scripts/review_harness, tests/test_review_harness.py and reviews/decisions.md on top of the PR head. For a PR that changes the harness, the reviewer therefore cannot run the PR's own tests or link-check the PR's decision log: here `git diff --cached` shows MD_LINK and the three new tests removed, pytest reports 83 (not 86), and the link checker reports bad 9 because main's decisions.md links 2026-10-22-pr6-fable.json, which is not in this checkout. This is the same gap as PR8-F6; the new evidence is the cause.
findings.evidence: review.yml:100-101: `git checkout -q origin/main -- REVIEW.md review scripts/review_harness reviews/decisions.md tests/test_review_harness.py tests/test_review_contract.py`. Staged diff in this checkout: respond.py loses MD_LINK; tests lose test_cells_quote_markdown_links_as_code, test_respond_workflow_reports_a_pushed_branch_without_a_pr, test_bytecode_is_ignored_and_untracked. `python -m pytest -q tests` -> 83 passed; `python3 tools/check_links.py .` -> `NOFILE ./reviews/decisions.md 2026-10-22-pr6-fable.json` x9, bad 9.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the protection, but give the reviewer a way to verify: have the workflow run `python -m pytest -q tests` and the link checker on a second, untouched checkout of the PR head (for example a `git worktree add $RUNNER_TEMP/pr pr-head`) and paste the two results into the material, or at least state in the material which files were replaced. Test: review a PR that adds a harness test and confirm the material shows the PR's own count.

findings.title: always() also runs the archive and artifact steps after a cancelled run
findings.claim: `always() && steps.respond.outputs.code == '0'` fires when the job is cancelled after the author step finished, so a cancelled run still pushes a response record to reviewer/archive and uploads an artifact for a response that was never opened as a PR.
findings.evidence: GitHub docs: `always()` runs the step even when the workflow is cancelled; `!cancelled()` runs it on success or failure only (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-when-your-workflow-runs/evaluating-expressions-in-workflows-and-actions#status-check-functions).
findings.proposed_change: Use `if: !cancelled() && steps.respond.outputs.code == '0'` on both steps and update the string asserted in test_respond_workflow_reports_a_pushed_branch_without_a_pr. Test: pytest, actionlint.

findings.title: MD_LINK leaves a stray '!' on image embeds and quotes links that would have resolved correctly
findings.claim: The regex matches the `[alt](src)` part of `![alt](src)`, producing `!`[alt](src)``; and it also quotes links the author writes relative to reviews/, such as `[BACKLOG.md](../BACKLOG.md)`, although the docstring's reason (they would resolve against the wrong folder) does not apply to those. Harmless, but the docstring overstates the reason.
findings.evidence: MD_LINK = `(?<!`)(\[[^\]\n]*\]\([^)\s]*\))(?!`)`: the lookbehind only excludes a backtick, not `!`. Traced by reading; could not run Python in this session.
findings.proposed_change: Either make the regex consume an optional leading `!` (`(?<!`)(!?\[...\]\(...\))(?!`)`) and say in the docstring that every quoted link becomes code, or leave the behaviour and reword the docstring to "links are shown as code rather than rendered". Add `![a](b)` and `[BACKLOG.md](../BACKLOG.md)` to test_cells_quote_markdown_links_as_code.

findings.title: CHANGELOG entry spans three physical lines; STYLE.md asks for one line per update
findings.checklist_item: Files: CHANGELOG.md — one line per update
findings.claim: Every earlier entry is a single line; this one is wrapped onto three with indentation. It renders as one bullet, but it breaks the file's convention and will sit awkwardly once main's two #6/#7 lines are merged in.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md lines 7-9 in the PR diff versus the single-line entries on lines 3-6.
findings.proposed_change: Join the entry into one line, and after merging main place it after the two 2026-10-22 lines from #6 and #7.
